Amendment 2 (model the main-loop hat on `closure.by`, with roster validation) is ratified in the same decision and is tracked as `closurebyroster` -- ratified, not deferred. The retroactive-meaning / forward-only-enforcement split below is ratified as written.

  *** THE ROW NAMED HERE, `closurebyroster`, HAS NEVER EXISTED IN THIS LEDGER. Found 2026-08-29 by following the cross-reference. ***  The sentence above ends "an amendment ratified in one place and tracked in another is how an obligation goes quiet" -- and it was attached to an obligation that had gone quiet, for exactly that reason.  THE REAL CARRIER IS `ledgerclosureby`, whose title is "closure.by holds the WRONG KIND of value on two rows, and a role distinction THE ROSTER DOES NOT MODEL on ten more" -- i.e. it already covers both halves of this amendment (the main-loop hat and roster validation).  What it did NOT carry was any record that it is discharging an OWNER-RATIFIED amendment rather than an ordinary records nit, which is the difference between an obligation and a tidy-up. state_semantics._WHY: The ledger's schema had NO WRITTEN SEMANTICS. That single absence is the cause behind six mis-counts in one session, two file-reading seats reading OPPOSITE conventions into one closure string, and five seats agreeing on only 4 of 11 rows they were asked to state-check. A field every round ranks and closes from was never defined.
state_semantics._THE_QUESTION_state_ANSWERS: Is anything still owed on this row, and who acts next?
state_semantics._TENSE: *** `state` IS PRESENT-TENSE; `closure.note` IS PAST-TENSE. *** The note is an EVENT LOG of what happened to a STAGE ('CLOSE (assess)' closes the assess stage). `state` asserts what the ROW still owes. **They are independent BY DESIGN** -- 23 rows share the string `CLOSE (assess)` across three states, and that is the ledger working correctly, not a defect: rows that experienced the same stage event legitimately differ in what else they owe. NEITHER can be derived from the other, and both attempts to do so have been measured wrong.
state_semantics.closed: Nothing outstanding; the claim was discharged BY WORK. Mechanical companions, era-scoped: commits, closure.by, and witness if closed on/after 2026-08-19.
state_semantics.dropped: Nothing outstanding; the claim was retired WITHOUT work, with the reason. Confusing this with `closed` is the es438 class -- both mean 'nothing owed', and misstating WHY is what misleads a future reader.
state_semantics.held: Something outstanding, waiting on a NAMED party or event, and carrying the QUESTION it is held for (standing rule). `open`/`held` WITH commits is normal here.
state_semantics._NOT_DERIVABLE_FROM: closure.note, entries, or stage coverage. Establishing a row's state requires a SUBSTANCE READ -- commits, gates, holds, filed questions -- which is what `asicbadaddr` was closed from and is the template.
state_semantics.open: Something outstanding, UNCLAIMED -- the complement of `in work`'s 'actively claimed'. No named party is required (that is `held`) and no work is under way. *** THIS DEFINITION WAS MISSING FROM THE BLOCK UNTIL 2026-08-25, AND `open` IS THE SECOND-LARGEST STATE IN THE LEDGER (46 of 216 rows). *** It appeared only inside `held`'s prose. Found by the fable5 adjudicator when asked to ratify the block -- it was told plainly that ratification was not wanted and to check the premises, and the gap is what that instruction bought. A checker built on the block as written would have misclassified a fifth of the ledger while reporting full coverage, which is this project's own 'a detector built from the wrong census reports full coverage' class wearing schema clothes.
state_semantics._RETROACTIVE_OR_FORWARD_ONLY: *** THE FIRST DRAFT SAID FORWARD-ONLY FLAT, AND THAT WAS HALF RIGHT IN THE LOAD-BEARING HALF. *** The split is by LAYER, and the block's own _TENSE ruling decides it: **the MEANING binds retroactively; only MECHANICAL CHECKS are forward-only by date.** `state` is PRESENT-TENSE, and a present-tense field has no era -- a false state is false NOW. 'Pre-adoption rows are read charitably' would preserve the exact defect this block exists to end (the es438 reader reads 'not done' off shipped, witnessed work TODAY) and would keep the ledger permanently bilingual. Forward-only enforcement follows the boilerplate-check precedent: a rule that retro-fails the archive gets disabled, and a disabled rule protects nothing. *** THE DISHONESTY WORRY DISSOLVES ONCE THE LAYERS ARE SEPARATED: `state` is a LIVE FIELD, NOT HISTORY. *** Correcting it rewrites no history -- `entries`, notes and `commits` are untouched. The migration is the warranted in-place repair already used twice on 2026-08-25: correct the state cell and attach a warrant note naming the row's OWN evidence. NO BULK REWRITE -- the round's central finding stands (state is NOT derivable; five seats agreed on only 4 of 11 rows), so every remaining row gets a substance read.

rows.state_note:
*** SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-08-27: THE DEFECT IS THE **WRITE HALF ONLY**, and saying the window 'bypasses the MMU ENTIRELY' reintroduces wording this row's title was already corrected away from. ***

**Why the unqualified form is wrong:** the round's own `sq miss evt` detector observes a **read-type TLB miss (`0x040`)** on the fixed build, so the read side is NOT unrouted. `memory_sh.c:290-301` carries the corrected scope.

> **THE CORRECT STATEMENT: no initial-page-write exception and no write-side protection check on stores into the SQ window.** The read/prefetch path translates; the store path does not. That asymmetry IS the defect, and it is narrower and more defensible than 'bypasses the MMU'.

**AND THE SECTION CITATIONS ARE BOTH RIGHT, FOR DIFFERENT THINGS -- reconciled here so the next reader does not have to choose:**
  * **section 3.6.7** *defines* the Initial Page Write exception and its code: *"occurs when the D bit is 0 even though a UTLB entry contains address translation information matching the virtual address to which a data access (write) is made... Sets exception code H'080 in EXPEVT."* (`sh7750_hardware.txt:9918-9928`)
  * **section 4.7.4, 'SQ Protection'** *applies* it to the store queues: *"Write type exception judgment is performed for writes to the SQs... a TLB miss exception, protection violation exception, or initial page write exception is generated."* (`:11742-11748`)
**The code cites 4.7.4; I cited 3.6.7. Cite BOTH -- 4.7.4 is the one that makes it apply to this window, and 3.6.7 is the one that says what the exception is.**

**Ranking, from today's adjudication: 7th of 8.** Latent -- no known guest depends on SQ write-protection. *It is a fidelity gap, not a live corruption, and my earlier 'most severe row in the batch' was severity within that batch, not across the queue.*

*** INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-27, and the step that could have KILLED it -- whether SH-4 exempts the store queue from translation -- goes the OTHER WAY. The manual refutes the exemption. (Already documented in-source and filed; today's work is re-verification.) ***

**THE BYPASS IS UNCONDITIONAL.** `memory_sh.c:353-357`:
```c
/*  Store queue region:  */
if (vaddr >= 0xe0000000 && vaddr < 0xe4000000) {
        /*  Note/TODO: Take SH4_MMUCR_SQMD into account.  */
        *return_paddr = vaddr;
        return 2;
}
```
**No `MMUCR.AT` test, no UTLB walk, no PR/D check**, and it returns 2 (read/write). `cpu_sh.c:106` is the only assignment of `translate_v2p`, and the sole SH consumer of `0xe0000000` in `src/cpus/` is `pref_rn` -- **no store instruction special-cases the window**, so every `mov.l Rm,@Rn` into it takes this branch. The preceding arm (`:339-350`) matches neither, so the path is identical with AT=1 and AT=0.

*** THE MANUAL SETTLES IT AGAINST THE EXEMPTION, from three directions: ***
  * **section 4.7.4, SQ Protection** (`sh7750_hardware.txt:11742-11748`): *"When MMU is on -- Operation is in accordance with the address translation information recorded in the UTLB, and MMUCR.SQMD. **Write type exception judgment is performed for writes to the SQs** ... a TLB miss exception, protection violation exception, or **initial page write exception** is generated."*
  * **section 4.7.3** (`:11691-11696`): *"the ASID, V, SZ, SH, PR, and D bits have the same meaning as for normal address translation."*
  * **QACR is explicitly the MMU-OFF-only mechanism** (`:11719-11723`, `:10473`), so it is NOT an alternative translation path under AT=1.

**AND PRIVILEGE DOES NOT RESCUE IT.** The Data TLB Protection Violation table (`:12632-12640`) gives `PR=00` as **"Only read access possible"** in PRIVILEGED mode, with EXPEVT `0x0A0` read / `0x0C0` write at `:12650`.

*** THE ASYMMETRY IS THE CLEANEST STATEMENT OF THE DEFECT: THE READ SIDE IS TRANSLATED AND THE WRITE SIDE IS NOT. *** The flush path at `cpu_sh_instr.c:3706-3765` explicitly checks `SH4_MMUCR_AT` and calls `sh_translate_sq_v2p()` -> `translate_via_mmu()`. The store path does none of it.

**WHY THE SHIPPED DETECTOR CANNOT SEE THIS, and it is not a detector defect:** `regress/sh_halt_probe.py:590-599` pins `sq pr00 evt` and `sq d0 evt` to **NOEXC deliberately** -- those rows exercise the read-type PREF path, where no protection or dirty case exists. **No row exercises the STORE side at all**, so the detector is silent here rather than contradicting the finding.

**ADJACENT, DISTINCT, ALREADY FILED:** the `SQMD` TODO on that same branch is a SECOND gap -- section 4.7.4 requires an ADDRESS ERROR for a user-mode SQ access when `MMUCR.SQMD = 1` even when translation succeeds, and the store path checks neither. `pref_rn` does check it (`cpu_sh_instr.c:3709-3715`) but raises `EXPEVT_RES_INST` instead -- filed as `sh4sqexpevt`.

*** EVIDENCE 2026-08-27: TRUE and GUEST-REACHABLE. A store into the store-queue window BYPASSES THE MMU, so page protection is not enforced on it. The most severe row in this batch. ***

**The mechanism:** the SQ write path does not go through `sh_translate_v2p()` / `translate_via_mmu()` (`memory_sh.c:353-357`, `:203-241`, with the source's own commentary at `:289-303`), so a store into the SQ window lands directly in the device's `sq` array.

**Guest access sequence, fully specified by the seat:**
  1. guest kernel enables paging (`MMUCR.AT = 1`);
  2. guest maps the SQ virtual page `0xe0000000` in the UTLB **valid** (`V=1`) and either **clean** (`D=0`) or **read-only** (`PR=00`);
  3. guest issues `mov.l r0, @r1` with `r1 = 0xe0000000`.

**Expected on hardware (SH7750 sections 4.7.4 / 3.6.7):** an **Initial Page Write** exception (`EXPEVT = 0x080`) on `D=0`, or a **Data Write Protection** exception on a read-only page.
**Actual here:** the store simply succeeds.

> **So a guest that maps a page read-only, or clean-for-dirty-tracking, and then stores through the SQ window gets a write that hardware would have faulted.** That is protection and dirty-bit tracking silently not enforced -- not a fidelity nit.

**Observable:** the guest `EXPEVT` register after the store -- `0x080` (or the write-protect code) when correct, unchanged when broken. Readable by an ordinary guest load, so no new probe capability is needed.

**CHECKABLE AGAINST A PRIMARY SOURCE WE HAVE:** the seat cites SH7750 sections 4.7.4 and 3.6.7, and `_scratchpad/sh7750_hardware.txt` is present and greppable. **Confirm the two sections before the round** -- and read the PROSE, not a figure, per the extraction rule.



*** PROMOTED BY THE CODEX RATING PASS, 2026-09-07, ON A ROW IT WAS NOT ASKED ABOUT -- and the
promotion is the answer to the brief's Q3, *what does my reading order miss?* ***

*"Promote `sh4sqwrite` ahead of the latent ASIC proposals.  Its title sounds like missing tests,
but `memory_sh.c` (anchor `Store queue region:`) grants read/write access directly, and `dev_sh4.c`
(anchor `DEVICE_ACCESS(sh4_sq)`) accepts the writes into queue storage.  Hardware requires
write-type exception checks on stores into those queues."*  (Renesas SH7750 manual, S4.7.4.)

> **THAT IS A GUEST-REACHABLE MISSING PROTECTION CHECK, not a coverage gap** -- and it was invisible
> to my keyword scan because the TITLE reads like harness debt.  *"No known guest depends on it"
> does not establish unreachability.*

**And the row's existing witness cannot carry it:** `sq pr00 evt` and `sq d0 evt` in
`regress/sh_halt_probe.py` exercise **PREF's READ-type judgement**, so they cannot witness a missing
STORE-side check.  A witness for this row has to drive a store.

*Filed as the strongest single finding of that pass; it needs a `sev` and a round of its own.*
rows.note:
*** 2026-09-11 -- NOW UNBLOCKED, AND IT IS THE BIGGEST MOVE IN THE COHORT. ***

Blocker verbatim: *a witness needs a build, which the machine embargo forbids*.  **Builds are routine; the embargo is gone, residue included.**

This row was **promoted 2026-09-07 by a codex rating pass on a row it was not asked about** -- *promote `sh4sqwrite` ahead of the latent ASIC proposals; hardware requires write-type exception checks on stores into those queues* -- and filed as **the strongest single finding of that pass, needing a `sev` and a round of its own.**

**And it needs no new probe capability:** its own note records that the observable is *readable by an ordinary guest load*.  **So the highest-value row in the cohort was fully unblocked and still carrying a blocker that suppressed it from every ranking.**

Replacement blocker text: *rung-3 witnessable -- a guest store through the SQ window, oracle EXPEVT, readable by an ordinary guest load.  No new capability and no blocker: this owes a ROUND, not a precondition.  Confirm SH7750 S4.7.4 / S3.6.7 from the PROSE, never a figure.*

*** 2026-09-11 ASSESS (codex GPT-6 Astra at max, 13,804 b).  **SUPPORTED** -- the first row tonight NOT refuted by its own assessment, and the finding is stronger than the filing. ***

*VERDICT: SUPPORTED at the translation/device layer: SQ fills omit write-type MMU checks.  Complete instruction-path reachability and external-memory consequences remain unverified.*

**`sh_translate_v2p()` handles the SQ window `0xe0000000-0xe3ffffff` by returning the original address with access result 2 (read/write available).  That branch consults NEITHER the write flag NOR MMU state, UTLB entries, PR, D, or privilege; it leaves `MMUCR.SQMD` an explicit TODO; and it RETURNS BEFORE the subsequent user-mode check** (`memory_sh.c:323-369`).  The window is registered to `dev_sh4_sq_access`, whose write branch copies bytes into the 64-byte queue with modulo indexing and returns success -- **no protection judgment, no exception dispatch** (`dev_sh4.c:2865-2867`, `:1574-1587`).

By comparison, ordinary MMU-translated U0/P0/P3 accesses enter `translate_via_mmu()`, deriving the access type from `FLAG_WRITEFLAG` and evaluating valid entries, VPN match, ASID, protection and dirty state: **PR 0/2 reject privileged writes; PR 1/3 permit writes only without an initial-write fault when D is set.**

> *** THE SQ-FILL PATH OMITS THE JUDGMENT RATHER THAN WEAKENING IT.  That is the load-bearing sentence: not a weaker rule applied, but no rule applied. ***

**THE MANUAL EXPRESSLY REQUIRES WRITE JUDGMENT WHEN FILLING THE QUEUES**, so this is a correctness gap rather than a defence-in-depth preference -- which is precisely the distinction that leaves `sh4itlbpr` unlicensed under the addition licence.  *These two SH rows look alike and are not.*

**A SECOND FUNCTION EXISTS AND DOES NOT SUPPLY THE CHECK:** `sh_translate_sq_v2p()` (`memory_sh.c:255-318`) forwards the caller's flags straight to `translate_via_mmu()`.  It neither forces read classification nor guards the ordinary SQ branch -- **and its actual caller is outside the permitted files, so whether it is wired at all is UNVERIFIED.**

**REACHABILITY IS SUPPORTED STRUCTURALLY, NOT CERTIFIED.**  The static chain is guest data access -> installed translation hook -> SQ identity mapping -> registered SQ device -> queue backing array, and all of it is guest-facing rather than debugger-only.  *The missing instruction and generic-memory implementations prevent certifying every link during actual instruction execution* -- stated as a limit rather than glossed.

**THE ROW'S "READABLE BY AN ORDINARY GUEST LOAD" CLAIM IS CONFIRMED:** EXPEVT sits at P4 `0xFF000024`, reachable by a privileged `MOV.L @Rm,Rn`, and the device's read case returns `cpu->cd.sh.expevt`.  **So no new probe capability is needed** -- which is what made this row the cheapest high-value item in the cohort.

*** BUT A LOAD FROM THE SQ APERTURE IS A DIFFERENT PROPOSITION, AND THIS IS THE CAUTION I WOULD HAVE MISSED: this emulator's SQ handler supports reads, while the manual defines architectural SQ readback ONLY for SH7750R, through a SEPARATE aperture `0xFF001000-0xFF00103C`.  "Such emulator readback cannot silently become a universal hardware oracle." ***

**STEPPING: SYNCHRONOUS, so a stepping probe is suitable in principle.**  The MMU failure path invokes `sh_exception()` directly with interrupt argument zero, and that function updates EXPEVT and transfers control **with no `single_step` guard**.  So the recorded suppression of ASYNCHRONOUS delivery does not disqualify this path.  **And `FLAG_NOEXCEPTIONS` is a separate mechanism that must not be conflated with `single_step`** -- a distinction this project has blurred before.

=== THE ORACLE, five wrong behaviours and what separates each ===
* **missing write check** -- the exception must be ATTRIBUTABLE to the tested access, with its fault address and saved instruction address;
* **wrong code** -- **exact EXPEVT comparison; reaching `VBR + 0x100` alone cannot distinguish protection, initial-write and several unrelated exceptions**;
* **write judgment applied to READS** -- a permitted read keeps read semantics, including no initial-write fault merely because D is clear;
* **faulting EVERY SQ store** -- permitted fills must complete and show their intended effect;
* **store never executed** -- *program liveness or an unchanged EXPEVT is INSUFFICIENT*; an old matching EXPEVT value, an unrelated exception, or a read without established execution all produce a FALSE PASS.

*** AND A VACUITY WARNING ABOUT A ROW THAT LOOKS SOUND: a passing READ control does NOT automatically kill a mutation at the SQ-fill guard ***, because `sh_translate_sq_v2p()` enters the common MMU helper directly and ordinary translated reads need not traverse the new guard at all.  Establishing that requires the omitted caller and the actual mutation site.

**SCOPE HELD, AND IT BOUNDS THE SEVERITY HONESTLY: this does NOT establish that an SQ fill overwrites protected external RAM.**  The operation changes queue SRAM; the external transfer is a SEPARATE operation.  No privilege escalation, no host compromise, no severity ranking and no runtime reproduction are claimed.

**STATUS: ready for a round.**  The defect is established at the translation and device layers, the observation register exists, the exception is synchronous, and the oracle is specified.  What is owed is the instruction-path link and the external-memory question -- both measurable.
